_note: Three device CLASSES, not three claims of reachability. `state` is the only field that says whether this round produced an observation: OBSERVED means a scan snapshot exists; NOT_OBSERVED means the authority knows the device id but no snapshot was supplied; UNRESOLVED means the authority declares no device id at all. A row with UNKNOWN must never be read as false.

devices.label: Windows (Dell-Company-PC)
devices.reason: The authority manifest declares device `dell-work` (os: windows) and records installations for it, but no observation snapshot for this device class was supplied in this round. Authority installation records are not an observation; mark the observation axes UNKNOWN rather than inferring them.

devices.label: Dell A6000 (Linux)
devices.reason: The authority manifest declares no device id for a Dell A6000 Linux node. Mapping it to `dell-work` would conflate a Windows device with a Linux one; the identity is UNKNOWN, so every device-dependent word is UNKNOWN rather than false.
